description: Duplicate detection (retrieve-then-judge): do two issues report the same underlying problem or request.

duplicate.instructions: Do `issue_a` and `issue_b` describe the same underlying problem or request, so that one could be closed as a duplicate of the other? A specific report of a more general issue counts as a duplicate unless something in the text points to a different cause. Similar topic or the same component alone is not enough.

state.issue_a: Since updating to 7.2 on my iPad, the PDF export of a project report produces a file where every page after the first one is blank. The first page looks fine, with the logo and the summary table. Pages two to five have the right headers and footers and page numbers, but the body area is completely white. Exporting the same report from the web app works. I tried smaller reports, and a two-page report has the same problem on page two.
state.issue_b: iOS app 7.2: exported PDFs only contain content on page 1. Our field team exports inspection reports from iPhones every day. Since the 7.2 update the PDFs have the correct number of pages and the page frame (header, footer, page x of y) on every page, but only page 1 has the actual report content; everything after it is empty. The same report exported from the browser is complete. Downgrading is not possible through the App Store, so we are currently exporting from laptops.

cases.rationale: Both describe 7.2 mobile PDF exports with empty pages after page one, nothing points to a different cause.

state.issue_a: Since Monday the mobile app sometimes shows 'Could not load projects' right after login. It happens for a few users in our Singapore office, mostly in the morning. Our network team checked and found that the corporate proxy there was updated on Monday and now strips the Authorization header on requests to your API domain, so the first request after login comes back 401 and the app shows the error. Users elsewhere are fine.
state.issue_b: Mobile app shows 'Could not load projects' after login for all our users, on every network, including mobile data. It started right after your release on Monday evening. Looking at the app logs, the projects request returns HTTP 500 with 'column projects.archived_at does not exist', so it looks like the API was deployed before the database migration ran. The web app shows the same error on the projects page, so nobody on our team can open any project at the moment.

cases.rationale: Same error message, but one is a proxy stripping headers for some users and the other a failed deploy for everyone: different causes.
